root_idea.summary: Aid, succour, and relief provided in a time of hardship.
root_idea.development: The root develops from assistance in distress into seeking aid, providing relief, cries for succour, and nouns naming aid or its provider. غَوْثٌ is also recorded as a tribal name.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form.
Displayed under the normalized Form X perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To aid, succour, or relieve someone from distress.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quran occurrence is the imperfect form يُغَاثُوا, expressing relief being provided; it occurs in a construction involving water described as like molten metal.

senses.definition: To seek, call for, or appeal for aid or relief.
senses.usage_conditions: The person or power appealed to may be expressed directly or with بِـ; seeking aid and calling for relief are constructional variations of the same use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cry out with an appeal for aid or succour, especially by uttering an exclamation of distress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form originally denotes the cry itself and is then used for calling out while seeking or demanding aid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cry out to one another for aid or succour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or mutual construction; it is also reported as synonymous with أَغَاثَ in another use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cry for aid or succour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun denoting the cry itself, distinct from the act of providing aid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Aid or succour; deliverance from difficulty, distress, adversity, or revenge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun or substantive associated with providing aid and release from hardship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An aider or succourer; one who provides aid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person or other agent regarded as a source of assistance.
An idiomatic name rather than a literal designation of aid.
A dialectal use attributed to Himyer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food or other succour supplied to a person in need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to the concrete means by which a needy person is assisted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vehemence of running; forceful or rapid running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical use reported in one textual reading.
Recorded as a plural said to have no singular form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Yaghūth, the name of an idol; alternatively, the name of a righteous man whose image later became an object of worship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper name associated with the ancient idols; no corresponding QAC form group is supplied for this proper-name item.
A tropical or figurative construction in which rain is the relieving agent; this is a broader Classical use, not the direct Quranic sense assigned here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a lute, to emit plaintive sounds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression applied to the sound of a lute.
A proper-name use distinct from the noun denoting a cry or aid.

cautions: The Quran-focused lexical discussion distinguishes الغَوْث, aid or succour, from الغَيْث, rain. It states that both اِسْتَغَاثُوا and يُغَاثُوا in 18:29 can be interpreted through either association; this artifact presents the غوث reading because the supplied QAC root is gwv.
The proper-name item يَغُوثُ is explicitly connected in the Classical evidence with a Quranic account, but no QAC form group or secure supplied word location is available for it here.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: For 18:29, the supplied Mufradat evidence leaves open whether اِسْتَغَاثُوا / يُغَاثُوا concerns seeking or receiving aid (غوث) or is connected with rain (غيث). The latter cannot be assigned as a direct gwv Quranic sense from the supplied packet.
